questions: What regular expression pattern should be used to identify words? The prompt says 'basic regular expression' but the reference uses r'\b\w+\b'. Should we follow that exactly, or is any pattern that splits on non-alphanumeric characters acceptable?
What encoding should be used when decoding the downloaded bytes? The reference uses .decode() without arguments, but text files could be in various encodings (UTF-8, Latin-1, etc.).

How should ties in word frequency be handled when selecting the top ten? The reference uses most_common(10) which returns the first ten encountered in case of ties, but other tie-breaking (alphabetical, arbitrary) could change the bar chart.
Should the bar chart have any specific styling (colors, bar width, rotation of x-axis labels, figure size)? The reference creates a basic chart, but unspecified details could vary.
What should happen if the URL returns an HTTP error (e.g., 404) or times out? The prompt mentions 'may not handle binary files' but not network errors.
Should the function close the matplotlib figure or leave it open? The reference returns the Axes object but doesn't specify figure lifecycle.
Are words containing apostrophes or hyphens (e.g., 'don't', 'state-of-the-art') considered single words or split? The regex \b\w+\b excludes punctuation, so they'd be split.
What should be returned if there are fewer than ten unique words? The reference would plot fewer bars, but is that acceptable, or should the chart still have ten bars (some zero)?
